texts: good. every participant is covered — the cleaning, the Keeper, the lantern's glass as a part of the lantern, the soft cloth as the means, and sundown as the time.
good. simple clause, Keeper and wick both covered, and the wick is correctly recorded as changed by the trimming.
good. the filling, the reservoir, the source flask and the day's ownership of it are all covered.

bad: the rule itself fires correctly, but "ground feathers" comes out as ONE feather rather than a set, and stating that the feathers are ground is what blocks the fix — a descriptive modifier on a plural has to be handed to each member separately, and there is no way to do that inside a conditional rule. Treat the ground feathers as a substance the way "salt-bloom" is treated in the next sentence, which parses cleanly: "When a station needs warding, the Keeper scatters ground-feather around the lantern." ("needs warding" and "around the lantern" are both fine as they stand — those are open questions on our side, not faults in your sentence.)
good. salt-bloom stays a substance and still records that it is a kind of bloom, "into the reservoir" is captured as the destination, and winter as the time.
good. Keeper, wick and the lighting are all covered, with the wick correctly recorded as changed.
